name: one-thing-sdk
description: OneThing turns a photo, a link or a picked product into a live one-product shop that takes PayPal payments, or a recommendation page that earns referral commissions through Channel3.  **How a shop is made** 1. `createShop`: start from a photo, a link, or a Channel3 product. Gemini guesses what it    is, how it's delivered, the price, a short link and the page design. You get back the    shop's link name and an **admin token**. 2. `updateShop`: correct anything the AI guessed, then set `status: live`. 3. Buyers pay on `https://<host>/<slug>` with PayPal. Sellers read orders and ship them.  **Auth.** Seller endpoints take the shop's admin token in the `x-admin-token` header, or a **platform API key** (`Authorization: Bearer ot_sk_…`) for marketplaces that make shops for their own sellers. Buyer endpoints (checkout, access-code verification, downloads) are public.  **Access codes.** A digital product can unlock an app or game instead of shipping a file. Each paid order gets a code such as `K7QF-M2XP-9HTD`; your app calls `verifyAccessCode` before unlocking. Raptor Rush on miriogames.com is a live example.  **Agent-ready.** Every live shop is also published for AI shopping agents: an MCP server at `/api/mcp` with `search_shops`, `get_product`, `create_order` and `get_order`, and the same four as plain GETs for assistants that can only fetch URLs (`listAgentShops`, `getAgentProduct`, `orderByLink`, `getAgentOrder`), with `/llms.txt` as the starting point. Order and status links also have short forms, `/<slug>/buy` and `/o/<order_id>/status`. An agent can find and order, but the buyer still approves every payment at PayPal.  **Limits.** Calls that cost something are capped per network: 120 checkouts per 10 minutes, 10 new shops an hour and 60 AI requests an hour. Over the cap the reply is a 429 with `Retry-After`.  All money moves through PayPal (sandbox in this deployment). OneThing never holds card data.
